course_name_original: Computación Numérica en Ingeniería de Datos

learning_outcomes.text: Know the appropriate mathematical concepts and methods to obtain models capable of solving problems that may arise in the context of data science and engineering: linear algebra, differential and integral calculus.
Evaluate the computational complexity of a problem and identify, if any, appropriate algorithmic strategies for its resolution.
Identify the limitations of common algebraic methods when applied to large, sparse, or structured matrices.
Know efficient methods for solving linear systems and for calculating the singular value decomposition of problems with large matrices.
Solve systems of non-linear equations, using the most appropriate method.
Identify and solve the multivariable interpolation problem.
Interpret and apply various methods of multivariable numerical integration.
Understand the numerical and discretization formulations of Fourier transform and finite difference problems.
Use software tools based on some of the methods studied and also use them as support tools for self-developed programs.

syllabus_topics: Linear Algebra Methods for massive data matrices. Methods for structured matrices.
Solutions of systems of non-linear equations. Multivariable interpolation.
Introduction to the finite difference method.
teaching_methods: Virtual expository sessions (videos, presentations, instructional texts, self-assessment questionnaires)
In-person expository classes (doubt resolution, theoretical development, examples)
Virtual laboratory practices (solving exercises with Matlab)
In-person laboratory practices (solving exercises with Matlab)
Tutoring (chat, forums, individual/group via Teams, in-person/virtual)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and participation in in-person activities
Virtual Campus activities and forum participation

assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call is calculated as NF = 0.2 MP + 0.5 NEx + 0.15 NA + 0.15 NCv, where MP is the project report, NEx is the exam grade on the project, NA is the attendance and in-class work grade, and NCv is the grade for Virtual Campus tasks. For NA to be considered, attendance of at least 80% of in-person sessions is mandatory. For differentiated evaluation, NA is replaced by NT (grade for mandatory tutorials). For extraordinary calls, two exams will be taken, one on theoretical-practical content and one on programming methods with Matlab, each weighing 50% of the final grade.
